articles.title: I Was Compelled to Revisit: Rory Kennedy on “Freefall: A Reckoning For Boeing”
articles.titleZh: 我被迫重新审视：罗里·肯尼迪谈《自由落体：波音的清算》
articles.author: Nell Minow

review.argument: Argument: it claims Boeing's shift to a profit-first model, rooted in the McDonnell Douglas merger and Jack Welch-style management, caused the crashes and ongoing safety failures, and that accountability has been evaded through legal and regulatory loopholes.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how corporate incentives and regulatory capture can override safety in any industry, and the reader gains a framework for questioning institutional assurances. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that Boeing's problems are systemic and that specific policy changes (like CEO accountability and FAA funding) could fix them.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a company people fly on, includes vivid scenes (the Barnett family's reaction, the Senate hearing), and has a hook (346 deaths, no apology).

zh.thesis: 波音在利润激励下牺牲安全，且至今未真正追责，是时候让监管和选举问责了。
paragraphs: 罗里·肯尼迪继《坠落：波音案》后推出续作《自由落体：波音的清算》。前作聚焦两起737 MAX坠机，346人遇难。波音起初归咎于飞行员，后来被迫承认是MCAS系统缺陷，却未受刑事追责。
复飞后事故不断，检举人约翰·巴内特在作证期间离奇死亡。更多吹哨人联系肯尼迪，促使她重返波音工厂内部，从他们的视角揭露质量管控被奖金激励的成本削减所取代。
对比1985年日航总裁亲自登门道歉，波音连电话致歉都欠奉。影片展现其持续缺乏人性，且董事会以短期股价为重，CEO薪酬上亿，公司却因短视决策亏损。
片中最敏感的是巴内特家人收到噩耗的瞬间，肯尼迪凭前作建立的信赖得以在场。她尽量少用重演，以档案为主，必要时用视觉手法区分虚构与真实。
参议院听证会上，议员用「可预防」「系统性」定性波音责任，但无人行动。肯尼迪呼吁：选一位工程师出身、重安全与卓越的CEO，司法部应追究刑责，并资助FAA、堵住旋转门。
所以，这不仅是航空安全控诉，更是对美国公司治理和监管失灵的清算。选举在即，选民应查清候选人是否支持监管机构，让决策者真正为346条生命担责。

en.thesis: Boeing's bonus-driven cost cutting has trashed safety without real accountability, so it's time for regulatory and electoral consequences.
paragraphs: Rory Kennedy follows her documentary 'Downfall: The Case Against Boeing' with 'Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing', revisiting the two 737 MAX crashes that killed 346 people. Boeing first blamed pilots, then admitted MCAS faults, but faced no criminal accountability.

After the planes returned to service, incidents piled up: engines falling off, windows blowing out. Whistleblower John Barnett died under suspicious circumstances while testifying. More whistleblowers reached out, prompting Kennedy to film inside Boeing's factories from their perspective.

Compared with the 1985 JAL crash, when the president personally apologized to victims' families, Boeing hasn't even called. The film shows a continued lack of humanity and a board rewarding short-term share prices; the CEO earned over $100 million, while the company lost money for the same reasons.

The most poignant scene captures the Barnett family receiving terrible news; Kennedy was trusted because of her prior work. She favors archives over re-enactments, distinguishing them clearly for authenticity.

At the Senate hearing, 'preventable' and 'systemic' were used, but nothing changed. Kennedy calls for an engineer-CEO focused on safety and excellence, criminal prosecution of executives, and proper funding for FAA oversight with a stop to the revolving door.

So this is more than an aviation safety complaint; it's a reckoning for US corporate governance and deregulation. With an election ahead, voters should research candidates' support for regulatory agencies, to make leaders answer for 346 lives.

articles.title: A joke domain purchase turned in geopolitical warfare
articles.titleZh: 从玩笑域名到地缘战争：SondeHub 的意外旅程
articles.author: kareiva

review.argument: Argument: it claims that a hobbyist radiosonde tracking site accidentally became a geopolitical asset, and that its open data is now used for military targeting, with the writer's own ethical dilemmas and decisions as evidence. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a benign tool's open data can be repurposed for warfare, and the reader sees the same pattern in other open data projects. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the narrative of how a joke domain escalated into a military data source, not just a list of events.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a real-world conflict (Ukraine), has a hook (a $439,000 missile vs a party balloon), and is readable cold with no background needed.

zh.thesis: 一个业余气球追踪网站意外成为军事和政府部门的数据源，甚至协助了反炮兵侦察和无人机袭击。
paragraphs: 2018 年，我注册了 sondehub.org，本来只是个玩笑，把访客重定向到 Habhub 的气象气球追踪页。但慢慢地，我们开始自己收集和提供数据，因为 Habhub 撑不住了。
我们的系统能追踪气球直至落地，还开发了「反向预测」：根据已升空气球的数据，反推其发射位置。这功能意外地揭示了军方炮兵阵地和舰船的位置——风数据不只用于气象，还用于火炮瞄准。
2023 年「中国间谍气球」事件后，我们的流量暴涨，收到了大量 .gov 和 .mil 的请求。2024 年底，有人开始滥用我们的 API 做预测，我们查到一个私有公司在用，但真正怀疑的是乌克兰军方用它规划无人机袭击。
我们紧急提供了本地跑预测器的方案，并联系 AWS，强调不要封禁该账号，避免造成伤亡。后来我们还收到了美国「战争部长办公室（情报与安全）」的数据请求，但我们开出账单后，对方从未付款。
我们还被 NTSB 联系，询问犹他州的气球与飞机相撞事件，我们提供了数据，最后确认是 Windborne 的气球。也收到过 FAA 的请求，解释气象气球的存在和法规——这不在我的预期内。
这些年还遇到过各种奇怪的事：有人捡到探空仪后撞车逃逸，我们帮忙找人；gpsjam.org 显示区域内有 GPS 干扰和欺骗；还收到过一位「奶酪占卜师」的采访请求。
总之，一个玩笑项目发展成了军事和民用机构都依赖的数据源，但也带来了伦理和法律问题：我们不想帮军方，但数据是公开的，只能从中尽量捞点基础设施维护费。这个故事还没完，这只是个开头。

en.thesis: An amateur balloon tracking site accidentally became a data source for military and government agencies, even aiding counter-battery and drone strikes.
paragraphs: In 2018 I registered sondehub.org as a joke, redirecting visitors to Habhub's weather balloon tracker. But gradually we started collecting and serving data ourselves, because Habhub was struggling.

Our system tracked balloons all the way to the ground, and we built 'reverse prediction': using data from a launched radiosonde to work backwards to its launch site. This unexpectedly revealed military artillery positions and ships—wind data isn't just for weather, it's also used for artillery ranging.

After the 2023 'China spy balloon' incident, traffic exploded and we got many .gov and .mil requests. In late 2024, someone started hammering our API for predictions; we found a private company, but our real suspicion was the Ukrainian military using it to plan drone strikes.

We rushed out a local predictor and contacted AWS, stressing not to block the account to avoid loss of life. Later we got a data request from the US 'Office of the Secretary of War (Intelligence and Security)', but they never paid the invoice we sent.

We also heard from the NTSB about a balloon-plane collision in Utah; we provided data and it turned out to be a Windborne balloon. The FAA asked us to explain weather balloons and regulations—not on my bingo card.

Through the years: a property owner asked us to find a hit-and-run driver who recovered a radiosonde, gpsjam.org showed GPS jamming and spoofing in the area, and we got an interview request from a 'cheese fortune teller'.

In short, a joke project became a data source both military and civilian rely on, but it raises ethical and legal questions: we don't want to help the military, but the data is public, so we might as well extract some funds for infrastructure. This story isn't over—this is just the beginning.

articles.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: 平庸之恶：AI 的毁灭潜能不是它的卖点，而是它的债务
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims that AI's destructive potential is being hyped by its own bosses as a marketing tactic, and that critics amplify this by treating AI as exceptional rather than normal, which helps the AI bubble grow. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how hype, even critical hype, can serve the hype's subject, and the reader can apply this to any overhyped technology or trend. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that criti-hype is a real phenomenon and that AI is normal, not exceptional.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a technology that affects jobs, climate, and the economy, it names specific actors (Altman, Sanders) and scenes (data centers, fired civil servants), and it has a hook: the idea that even critics are helping the hype. Readable cold.

zh.thesis: AI 并非例外之物，它只是普通技术，我们不该被其「毁灭潜能」的炒作所裹挟。
paragraphs: AI 老板们喜欢谈论自家产品的可怕潜力：取代工作、觉醒成纸夹。这看着像担忧，其实是炫耀，因为 AI 现在只靠「潜力」活着。
真实的 AI 只是边际有用，像个插件，可能帮你，也可能没用。它是普通技术，但普通技术不值得万亿投资和公务员大换血。
AI 的毁灭性是真实的，但它在别处：解雇员工换聊天机器人、数据中心泡沫、水和电的巨量消耗。这才是我们该抨击的毁灭。
别再重复炒作。「AI 安全」「流氓 AI」？该问的是为什么安全工具连沙箱都建不好。AI 不邪恶，它只是计算机，能触发脆弱，但不是诅咒。
把 AI 当例外，就是给平庸之辈加冕。Sam Altman 是骗子，不是魔王，夸大他的邪恶只会帮他融资。
正确的批评是指出他们在说谎，而不是把谎言当警告复述。这就是所谓的「批评式炒作」。
所以，把 AI 当普通技术吧。用它，或者不用，你都不会被传染。真正该做的是在 AI 公司破产时，买下服务器开开放模型。

en.thesis: AI is not exceptional; it's a normal technology, and we shouldn't be swayed by the hype of its 'destructive potential'.
paragraphs: AI bosses love to talk about their products' terrible potential: taking our jobs, waking up, turning us into paperclips. It looks like concern, but it's a boast, because right now AI lives on 'potential' alone.
Real AI is only marginally useful, like a plugin that might help, might not. It's normal technology, but normal tech doesn't warrant a trillion in investment and mass firings of civil servants.

AI's destructiveness is real, but it's elsewhere: firing people for chatbots that can't do the job, the data-center bubble, the massive water and energy use. That's the destructiveness we should attack.

Stop repeating the hype. 'AI safety' and 'rogue AI'? The right question is why their security tools can't even build a proper sandbox. AI isn't evil; it's just computers that can trigger vulnerabilities, not curses.
Treating AI as exceptional crowns mediocrities. Sam Altman is a con man, not a super-villain, and exaggerating his evil only helps him raise money.
The right criticism is to point out they're lying, not to repeat their lies as warnings. That's what's called 'criti-hype'.
So treat AI as normal. Use it or don't; you won't be infected. The real move is to buy the servers at pennies on the dollar when the companies go bankrupt and run open models.

articles.title: What Happens If OpenAI Dies?
articles.titleZh: 如果 OpenAI 死了会怎样？
articles.author: Ed Zitron

review.argument: Argument: it claims OpenAI's economics are so ruinous that its collapse is a real possibility, and traces the specific obligations, funding gaps, and counterparty risks that could trigger it. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a company can make commitments so large that its survival depends on perpetual fundraising, and the reader sees the same pattern in other bubble industries. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, the numbers, and the skepticism about annualized revenue and media complicity.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and the future of a company everyone has heard of, it has a hook (OpenAI losing $20.9 billion on $13 billion revenue), and it is readable cold despite the jargon.

zh.thesis: OpenAI 的财务承诺和亏损不可持续，如果 Anthropic 先上市，OpenAI 将难以生存。
paragraphs: OpenAI 近期完成了 70 亿美元的内部股票回购，却在同一周失去了 COO 和 CRO。CRO 上任仅八个月就离职，说明内部对上市前景已经动摇。
OpenAI 的对手 Anthropic 正在筹备上市，估值传闻高达 2 万亿美元。但它的财报同样难看，收入增长靠补贴和客户烧钱，实际亏损巨大。
OpenAI 的处境更糟：2025 年亏损 209 亿美元，收入仅 130.7 亿。它需要每年融资 1000 到 2000 亿美元，但主要投资者软银、亚马逊、英伟达都已显疲态。
OpenAI 还欠着超过 8000 亿美元的算力承诺，仅云服务费就到 2027 年需支付 1460 亿美元。它必须在 2030 年前收入翻十倍并实现盈利，几乎不可能。
如果 OpenAI 倒闭，微软可能吸收它，或者它被迫与 Anthropic 合并。但更可能的是，它成为整个 AI 泡沫的替罪羊，拖垮软银和众多依赖它的公司。

en.thesis: OpenAI's financial commitments and losses are unsustainable, and if Anthropic goes public first, OpenAI's survival is in doubt.
paragraphs: OpenAI recently completed a $7 billion share buyback, yet lost its COO and CRO in the same week. The CRO left after just eight months, signaling internal doubts about an IPO.
Rival Anthropic is preparing for an IPO, with valuations rumored at $2 trillion. But its financials are equally ugly, with revenue growth driven by subsidies and customer burn, masking huge losses.
OpenAI is worse: it lost $20.9 billion in 2025 on revenue of $13.07 billion. It needs to raise $100-200 billion annually, but key backers like SoftBank, Amazon, and NVIDIA are showing strain.
OpenAI has over $800 billion in compute commitments, with $146 billion in cloud bills due by 2027. It must decuple revenue and become profitable by 2030—an almost impossible task.
If OpenAI collapses, Microsoft might absorb it, or it could merge with Anthropic. More likely, it becomes the scapegoat for the AI bubble, dragging down SoftBank and countless dependent companies.

articles.title: Pluralistic: IP can't save you from AI (18 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: IP 救不了你对抗 AI
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims copyright cannot protect creative workers from AI because it grants rights without leverage, and uses the Spirit Airlines data sale to Google as evidence that property rights fail where labor and privacy rights are needed. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how legal rights without bargaining power fail workers, and the reader can apply it to any industry facing automation. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that copyright expansion is a losing strategy, not just the news about Spirit.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about jobs and privacy, has a concrete scandal (Spirit data sold to Google), and is readable cold with no background.

zh.thesis: 版权扩张救不了创意工作者，劳动力权和隐私权才是根本。
paragraphs: 你不需要相信 AI 艺术有任何价值，也能看出资本为什么疯狂投钱：他们相信可以用 AI 替换掉所有行业的工人。艺术家也是工人，想保护自己的劳动利益。
但很多同行认为，办法是扩大版权，让爬取互联网、分析作品、用来训练 AI 变成非法。这是个必输的策略。
首先，禁止爬取或分析会造成巨大的附带伤害。从《牛津英语词典》到搜索引擎，再到互联网档案馆，都依赖版权允许的语料收集和分析。想写一部只禁止 AI 训练、不伤及无辜的法律，几乎不可能。
更关键的是，版权给不了你议价能力。版权是「准财产权」，可以分拆出售，但你要有筹码、有其他选择，才能谈到好价钱。而创意产业高度垄断，公司越来越大，艺术家越来越穷。
版权扩张只让老板更富。真正有用的是劳动权，比如编剧工会通过罢工赢得了对抗 AI 的胜利。但老板们其实希望用 AI 来压低工资，他们状告 AI 公司，也只是想分走你的那份损失。
今天有个最清楚的例子：Spirit 航空破产后，受托人把全体员工的所有邮件、日程、文件卖给了 Google 用来训练 AI。这些私人信息，员工自己毫无控制权。
版权和隐私、劳动权不是一回事。隐私法在美国几乎死光了，劳动法也不保护你在工作设备上的私人数据。想要真正对抗 AI，就得争取集体谈判和全面的隐私权，而不是指望版权。

en.thesis: Copyright expansion won't save creative workers; labor rights and privacy rights are the only real protection.
paragraphs: You don't have to believe AI art has any value to see why capital is pouring in: they think they can replace every kind of worker with AI. Artists are workers too, and we want to protect our labor interests.
But many of my peers think the answer is to expand copyright, to make scraping, analyzing, and publishing the analysis of copyrighted works illegal. That is a losing strategy.

First, banning scraping or analysis would cause enormous collateral damage. The OED, search engines, and the Internet Archive all rely on the legal ability to collect and analyze a massive corpus. Writing a law that only stops AI training and spares the beneficial uses is nearly impossible.

More fundamentally, copyright doesn't give you bargaining power. It's a pseudo-property right, divisible and sub-licensable, but to negotiate well you need leverage and options. And after decades of lax antitrust, the creative industries are boiled down to a handful of giants; artists are poorer than ever.

Copyright expansion has only enriched the bosses. What works is labor rights: the Writers Guild beat AI with a strike. But the studios, not AI companies, wanted to replace writers, and their lawsuits against AI firms are just a fight over who gets your lost wages.

Today's clearest example: after Spirit Airlines went bankrupt, the trustees sold all employees' emails, memos, and calendar entries to Google for AI training. These are deeply private messages, and the workers have no control over them because they signed 'works made for hire' agreements.

Privacy law in America is nearly dead, and labor law doesn't protect your personal data on work devices. To really fight AI, we need collective bargaining and comprehensive privacy rights, not copyright.

articles.title: If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast
articles.titleZh: 如果这是真的，超大云厂商就完了
articles.author: Joachim Klement

review.argument: Argument: it claims SLMs on local devices already match or beat cloud LLMs in most tasks, making hyperscaler data-center capex a likely waste, and cites a Stanford study with win/tie ratios and cost figures. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a cheaper, local alternative can undercut a centralized infrastructure bet, and the reader can apply it to other tech shifts. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that data centers are the wrong investment, not just the study's numbers.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and a technology the reader uses, has a startling number (98.6% win/tie, $10tn market), and is readable cold.

zh.thesis: 斯坦福的研究表明，小语言模型在本地运行已能取代大语言模型的大部分任务，云巨头们的巨额投资可能打水漂。
paragraphs: 斯坦福大学五月发表的研究比较了在本地电脑上运行的小语言模型（SLM）和数据中心里的大语言模型（LLM）。结果显示，在聊天任务中，最好的 SLM 在 98.6% 的情况下能和 LLM 打平或更好。
推理任务上 SLM 也在快速追赶，平均 62.5% 的情况不输 LLM。按真实任务比例加权后，SLM 在 81.2% 的情况下能与 LLM 持平或胜出，只在工程、生命科学等领域明显落后。
而且 SLM 的能耗和计算成本比 LLM 低 50% 到 85%。推理每瓦特的效率是 LLM 的七倍。这意味着，凡是能在本地解决的任务，送数据中心反而更贵。
如果这个趋势持续，我们需要的数据中心会少得多。报告估计美国 SLM 的可用市场已达 10 万亿美元，相当于美国 GDP 的三分之一。LLM 的生存空间正在被压缩。
作者认为，数据中心可能是当前 AI 领域最糟糕的投资。真正的赢家或许是戴尔、苹果这类桌面电脑制造商。Nvidia 若能用消费级芯片替代高端数据中心 GPU，其利润和增长前景将面临巨大压力。

en.thesis: Stanford research shows small language models running locally can now replace large ones for most tasks, threatening the hyperscalers' massive investments.
paragraphs: A Stanford study published in May compared small language models (SLMs) running on local PCs with large language models (LLMs) in data centers. In chat tasks, the best SLMs matched or beat LLMs in 98.6% of cases.

They are also catching up fast on reasoning, matching or exceeding LLMs in 62.5% of cases. Weighted by real task mix, SLMs match or beat LLMs 81.2% of the time, only clearly behind in fields like engineering and life sciences.
And SLMs use 50% to 85% less energy and compute. Their inference per watt is seven times higher. So anything solvable locally is cheaper to run there than in the cloud.
If this trend holds, we'll need far fewer data centers. The report estimates the U.S. addressable market for SLMs at $10 trillion, a third of GDP. The space left for LLMs is shrinking.

The author argues data centers may now be the worst AI investment. The real winners could be boring desktop makers like Dell and Apple. If Nvidia shifts to consumer chips, its margins and growth will suffer.

articles.title: Why I'm Staying Out Of The Substack Religion Debate
articles.titleZh: 为什么我不参与 Substack 上的宗教论战
articles.author: Scott Alexander

review.argument: Argument: it claims that theism's 'divine simplicity' defense is a sleight of hand that subtracts limits rather than complexity, and that theism must face the same preemptive penalty as alien-conspiracy explanations. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a 'powerful hidden entity' explanation can be optimized to evade every disconfirmation, and the reader recognizes the pattern in conspiracy theories and other domains. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the citations.
review.appeal: +8 — it has a vivid hook (the Napoleon-aliens analogy), a concrete target (Adelstein's argument), and a memorable reframing of simplicity, though it is dense and assumes some familiarity with philosophical debate.

zh.thesis: 对宗教的怀疑植根于一种先于论证的本能，而不是可以靠精确推理得出的结论。
paragraphs: 最近 Substack 上满是上帝存在与否的辩论，Adelstein、Chappell 等一票人马在一个月内接连下场。我年轻时也热衷此道，现在却提不起兴致，因为我的无神论直觉似乎先于所有具体论证。
打个比方：假如有个社会郑重其事地争论「外星人是否协助拿破仑崛起」，反对者会列举很多理由——他以少胜多、称帝于反君主制浪潮之后——但这些都可以用「强大外星人暗中干预」来回应。
这种解释其实比正常解释更「好用」，因为它能解释一切。但我们不会认真对待它，靠的不是精确计算贝叶斯概率，而是常识直接排除。我的无神论正是这种「先排除」的本能。
这听起来危险，像「荒谬性启发法」，可能误伤真正的新事物，比如 1900 年的核武器。它也无助于说服信徒。所以关键问题是：为什么我们本能地排除「外星人助拿破仑」？
答案是过拟合。任何异常都可以归因于「有强大隐藏实体刻意促成此事」，这种解释太灵活，必须预先惩罚。通常的惩罚叫「阴谋论」，但外星人版本规避了人类共谋的弱点，反而更危险。
历史上，每当人们遇到无法解释的现象，就编造这类解释，比如雷神、太阳神。科学进步后，这些解释被逐一放弃。如今剩下的异常——宇宙存在、意识、微调等——有人又套用同一模板。
所以，在听任何论证之前，我已经本能地翻白眼。这个直觉性排除，比任何精细推理都更根本。

en.thesis: My atheism rests on a pre-argumentative intuition, not on any conclusion I reached by precise reasoning.
paragraphs: Substack has lately been full of debates over God's existence, with Adelstein, Chappell, and a dozen others all jumping in within a single month. I enjoyed that in the early 2000s, but now I can't muster the interest, because my lack of belief feels like it precedes all the specific arguments.

Consider a society that seriously debates whether aliens helped Napoleon rise. Proponents note his strange victories against overwhelming odds and his crowning right after France swore eternal enmity to monarchy. But all of that can be met with 'powerful aliens secretly intervened.'

That explanation is actually more flexible than the normal one, so it can explain anything. Yet we never take it seriously, not because we compute probabilities, but because common sense rules it out upfront. My atheism is that kind of preemptive exclusion.

That sounds dangerous, like the 'absurdity heuristic,' which would have dismissed nuclear weapons in 1900 and heavier-than-air flight in 1850. It also cannot convince believers, because religion does not feel absurd to them. So the real question is: why do we instinctively exclude the Napoleon scenario?

The answer is overfitting. Any anomaly can be explained by 'a powerful hidden entity intended that specific thing,' and that flexibility demands a penalty. We usually apply that penalty under the label 'conspiracy theory,' but the alien version dodges the usual objections about human collaboration, which makes it even more worrying.

Historically, whenever people met something they could not explain, they invented such accounts, like thunder gods and sun gods. Science pushed those back one by one. Now the remaining anomalies—existence, consciousness, fine-tuning—are being met with the same template.
So before I even hear the arguments, my eyes roll. That instinctive exclusion is more fundamental than any delicate reasoning.

articles.title: An LLM wiki changed how I work
articles.titleZh: LLM 维基如何改变我的工作方式
articles.author: Casey Newton

review.argument: Argument: it claims that an LLM wiki, a self-organizing knowledge base built from personal archives and daily clippings, is the most useful productivity tool the author has adopted, and it details the setup, maintenance costs, and benefits. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a personal knowledge base can be automated to surface connections and story ideas, which applies to any knowledge worker, not just tech reporters. The reader gains a concrete, replicable workflow idea.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one — the author argues that the maintenance burden is worth the payoff, and that this is the 'teleological end' of personal knowledge management. Delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the description.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a tool that could change how the reader manages their own research and notes, it includes a concrete scene (the author checking the wiki each morning), and it has a hook (Karpathy's tweet as an 'infohazard').

zh.thesis: LLM 维基能自动整理个人知识库，虽需维护，但比以往任何系统都更省时、更有用。
paragraphs: 四月初，Andrej Karpathy 发推说，他正用 LLM 把资料整理成本地 Markdown 维基，随加随新。这个想法很快传开，我也立刻决定要试。
我先是把 Platformer 的全部存档喂进去，Claude 把里面的人物、公司、概念抽出来，写成了维基页面。现在我有 1440 多个页面，连我的 Meta 页都超过 1.2 万字。
每天早晨，我用 Obsidian 的剪藏工具把新闻存进去，脚本自动归类。它还会生成概念页，比如「tokenmaxxing」「AI 版权」，并更新首页。
这种系统对复杂事件特别有用。像 OpenAI/Hugging Face 代理事件，我每天写稿前先看维基页，对照原始来源，确保没说错，省了大量时间。
不过它也麻烦：页面太长要压缩，代码出错要修，Claude 的风格太浓缩，我后来用 GPT-5.6 Sol 重写了。
即便如此，我觉得这是自 2008 年用 Evernote 以来，我一直想要的知识库。尽管不够精巧，但它是这类工具的必然方向。

en.thesis: An LLM wiki that auto-organizes a personal knowledge base is worth the upkeep, saving more time than any system before it.
paragraphs: In early April, Andrej Karpathy tweeted that he was using LLMs to build local Markdown wikis from source documents, updated as he added material. The idea spread fast, and I decided to try it.
I seeded mine with my entire Platformer archive. Claude extracted people, companies, and concepts into wiki pages. Now I have more than 1,440 pages, including a Meta page over 12,000 words.

Each morning I clip news into Obsidian, and a script sorts it. It generates new pages for concepts like 'tokenmaxxing' or 'AI copyright', and updates a home page. It has replaced my old 'blips' system.
It has been a boon for complex, fast-moving stories like the OpenAI/Hugging Face breach. Each day I pull up the page, refresh my memory, and check original sources to avoid hallucinations.
But it demands upkeep: pages grow too long, scripts break, and Claude's compressed style needed rewriting. For that I used GPT-5.6 Sol.
Still, it is the culmination of my search for a self-organizing knowledge base, something I have sought since Evernote in 2008. It may be clunky, but it is the teleological end of such tools.

articles.title: Why You Move Factors in to Whether It Protects You From Dementia
articles.titleZh: 为什么要运动，以及它是否能预防痴呆，都取决于运动的场景
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the protective effect of physical activity on dementia depends on context, with leisure activity reducing risk and occupational activity increasing it, and it offers mechanisms for the paradox. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is that the same behavior can have opposite health effects depending on context, which applies to how the reader thinks about work versus leisure in their own life. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that context matters, not just the study's findings.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a health risk people live with, it contradicts the simple 'exercise is good' assumption, and it is readable cold with a clear hook.

zh.thesis: 运动是否降低痴呆风险取决于它是休闲还是工作，休闲运动降低风险，体力劳动反而升高。
paragraphs: 早就知道规律运动能降低痴呆风险。但《柳叶刀·公共卫生》新发表的荟萃分析给这个结论加了前提：关键在运动的场景。
研究覆盖 420 多万成年人，发现休闲运动（跑步、骑车、打球）能把痴呆风险降低 24%，而体力要求高的工作反倒让风险升高 20%。这就是所谓的「体力活动悖论」。
原因还不完全清楚。休闲运动通常让人放松、减少压力，还常伴随社交，这些都有保护作用。而体力工作重复单调、恢复时间少，还暴露在噪音和空气污染里，可能都伤脑。
研究只是观察性的，不能下因果结论。但它和上月那篇「坐着时动脑比看 TV 好」的发现一致：不管动不动，场景才是关键。所以，改善公园和步道、保障闲暇时间、减少工作风险，可能比单纯鼓励运动更重要。

en.thesis: Whether exercise protects against dementia depends on whether it's leisure or work: leisure lowers risk, physical labor raises it.
paragraphs: It has long been known that regular exercise is linked to lower dementia risk. But a new meta-review in The Lancet Public Health adds a caveat: it depends on the context.

Looking at over 4.2 million adults, the researchers found that leisure-time activity (running, cycling, sports) cut dementia risk by 24 percent, while physically demanding jobs raised it by 20 percent. This is the 'physical activity paradox'.

The reasons are still murky. Leisure activity is relaxing and reduces stress, and it often comes with socializing, both protective. Physically demanding jobs, by contrast, are repetitive, allow little recovery, and expose workers to noise and air pollution—all potential contributors.

The study is observational, so it can't prove causation. But it matches last month's finding that thinking while sitting beats watching TV. Either way, context is key. So improving access to parks and trails, ensuring leisure time, and reducing workplace hazards may matter as much as promoting exercise itself.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Text Watermarking Proves AI Companies Do Not Care at All About Writing
articles.titleZh: Anthropic 的文本水印证明 AI 公司根本不在乎写作
articles.author: Jason Koebler

review.argument: Argument: it claims Anthropic's watermarking scheme reveals the company treats word choice as fungible and writing as a probabilistic game, and it grounds that claim in Anthropic's own blog post and the SynthID study's quality metrics. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a tech company's engineering mindset flattens a human craft into interchangeable tokens, and the reader comes away seeing AI text and its makers differently. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that Anthropic's 'low-stakes' synonym choices are not low-stakes, backed by the contrast between 'grey' and 'overcast' and the thumbs-up quality metric.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about something people live with (AI writing, the value of human expression), it has a concrete hook (the 'cold and grey' vs 'cold and overcast' example), and it is readable cold.

zh.thesis: Anthropic 对文本水印的解释暴露出它把词语视为可互换的，这从根本上贬低了写作。
paragraphs: Anthropic 宣布未来版本的 Claude 生成文本时会带上水印，用来标记 AI 生成的内容。最近它发文解释了实现方式：不添加任何字符，而是悄悄改变用词，只有它的算法能识别。
Anthropic 举例说「天气寒冷而灰暗」和「天气寒冷而阴沉」这两种说法对读者区别不大，所以此时用哪个词就由随机数决定。水印就是利用这类「低风险」选择留下模式。
但任何写过东西的人都知道，「灰暗」和「阴沉」并非总是可以互换。作者选哪个词，可能取决于风格、情绪、经历，甚至是三年级老师常说的那个词。Anthropic 却把这种选择看作随机事件。
Anthropic 声称水印不影响输出质量，内部测试也未见内容、创意或可读性下降。但它的质量评估方式很可疑：参考的 Google 研究只是让用户在聊天界面点赞或点踩，这能衡量「写作质量」吗？
水印技术本身可能有用，但它暴露了 AI 公司对写作的态度：词语是随机数生成器挑的，是可替换的零件，而不是表达思想的工具。这比水印本身更令人担忧。
所以问题的根源不是水印，而是 AI 写作本身就被视为概率游戏。Anthropic 不在乎文字背后的工匠精神，只把它当作需要标记的产物。这提醒我们，人类写作中的每一个字都有意义，而这正是 AI 永远无法模仿的。

en.thesis: Anthropic's explanation of text watermarking reveals it treats words as interchangeable, fundamentally devaluing writing.
paragraphs: Anthropic has announced that future versions of Claude will watermark the text it generates. It has now explained how: nothing is added to the text and no hidden characters, but the word choices are subtly altered in a way only its algorithm can detect.

Anthropic gives an example: 'The weather today was cold and grey' versus 'The weather today was cold and overcast.' It claims these choices are low-stakes and settled by a random number, and watermarking uses such choices to leave a detectable pattern.

But anyone who has written anything knows 'grey' and 'overcast' are not always interchangeable. A writer might choose one over the other based on style, mood, or a memory. Anthropic treats this as random, showing a deep misunderstanding of writing.

Anthropic insists watermarking doesn't affect output quality, citing internal tests. But the quality assessment it relies on comes from a Google study where users simply gave thumbs up or down to chatbot responses. That hardly measures the quality of writing.

Watermarking might be useful, but it exposes how AI companies see words: as fungible parts chosen by a random number generator, not as tools for expressing thought. That mindset is more troubling than the watermark itself.

So the real problem is not the watermark but what it reveals. Anthropic doesn't care about the craft of writing, only about labeling its output. It reminds us that every word a human writes carries meaning, and that is something AI can never reproduce.

articles.title: The Wonders of the Male Human Pelvis
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the male human pelvis has a unique forward-oriented hip socket configuration that improves walking efficiency, and contrasts it with the female pelvis constrained by childbirth. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how evolutionary trade-offs shape bodies differently, and the reader can apply it to thinking about sex differences and adaptation. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the study summary.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about the reader's own body, has a surprising hook (male pelvis overlooked), and is readable cold, though it stays at a distance.

zh.thesis: 男性骨盆的独特构造是为了更高效地行走，而女性因生育需求无法发展出这种结构。
paragraphs: 关于女性骨盆的研究很多，因为分娩困难与直立行走、头颅大小等进化权衡有关。相比之下，男性骨盆一直被忽视，直到现在。
《科学报告》上的一项新研究分析了 91 个现代人类骨盆和两个尼安德特人男性骨盆，发现现代男性骨盆的髋臼更朝前，这有助于行走。
行走就像一连串受控的跌倒：身体失去平衡，再迈腿接住自己。每次下落都会冲击关节，也需要能量恢复。男性骨盆让腿更靠前，股四头肌既能吸收冲击，又能弹回身体，走路更省力。
研究者认为，这种高效步态可能让男性在长距离上有优势。而女性骨盆因生育限制没能发展出这些改变。这些发现还能帮助生物力学、康复医学等研究。

en.thesis: The male pelvis is uniquely shaped for efficient walking, and females could not develop it because of childbirth demands.
paragraphs: There is plenty of research on the female pelvis, for good reason: the obstetrical dilemma ties childbirth to evolutionary trade-offs, upright walking, and skull size. The male pelvis, by contrast, has been overlooked—until now.

A new study in Scientific Reports looked at 91 modern human pelvises and two Neanderthal male ones, and found the modern male pelvis has hip sockets oriented more to the front, an adaptation for walking.

Walking is a series of controlled falls: you lose balance, then swing a leg forward to catch yourself. Each drop jars your joints and costs energy. The male pelvis puts the legs slightly forward, so the quads both absorb the shock and spring the body back up, making the gait more efficient.

That may give men an edge over long distances, while childbirth constraints kept women from evolving the same. The findings also feed into biomechanics, rehabilitation, and injury prevention, the authors note.

articles.title: The Generalizability Problem, the Natural Field Experiments Answer
articles.titleZh: 一般化问题，自然现场实验的回答
articles.author: conversableeconomist

review.argument: Argument: it claims the generalizability problem in social science is best answered by natural field experiments, and uses Scared Straight's failure to show why lab or pilot results mislead. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a result from one context can fail when scaled, and the reader sees why testing in real life beats trusting a pilot. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument for natural field experiments, not just a summary of List's work.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about how policies and programs work in the real world, has a vivid example (Scared Straight), and is readable cold.

zh.thesis: 社会科学的结论难以直接推广，自然现场实验是应对这一问题的有效方法。
paragraphs: 社会科学有个老问题：小规模研究的结论能推广到多大范围？一个学区有效的项目，换到别的学区、州、国家还有用吗？这问题没有简单答案。
约翰·李斯特给出了一个角度，他举了「吓直」项目的例子：美国 30 多个州用囚犯吓唬问题少年，试点时效果很好，80% 到 90% 的参与者没再惹事，但推广后却失效了，有些地方的犯罪率还上升了。
李斯特主张用自然现场实验来应对。参与者在不知情的情况下被研究，比如审计研究里，研究员派不同种族的助手去租房、求职，对方并不知道自己在被测试。这需要伦理审批，且不能让参与者承受额外负担。
他当了沃尔玛的首席经济学家后，带着团队和 6000 多个供应商做实验，测试怎样最有效地激励他们减排。这个思路说明，世界上的自然现场实验应该更多。

en.thesis: Social science findings are hard to generalize, and natural field experiments are a practical answer.
paragraphs: Social science has a familiar problem: how far do small-study results reach? A program that works in one school district — would it work in another, statewide, nationally, in other countries? There is no simple answer.

John List offers his angle. He cites Scared Straight, a program that took at-risk teens to meet maximum-security prisoners. A pilot was wildly successful, 80–90% of participants stayed clean, but scaled up it flopped, and crime sometimes rose.

List's answer is natural field experiments, where participants don't know they're being studied. Audit studies are a classic: researchers send assistants with similar résumés but different races to rent apartments or apply for jobs, and the landlords or employers never know.

These need ethics approval and shouldn't push participants beyond their normal choices. Now at Walmart, List's team runs experiments with over 6,000 suppliers to test what best cuts their carbon. His point: the world has far too few such experiments.

articles.title: Arabic has four words for sadness. Philosophy explains why
articles.titleZh: 阿拉伯语有四个词表示悲伤。哲学解释了为什么
articles.author: Chereen Shurafa

review.argument: Argument: it claims Arabic's four sadness words encode distinct philosophical stances on grief, and that this lexical richness reflects a cultural tradition of analyzing emotion rather than merely naming it.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a language's vocabulary shapes and reveals a culture's way of thinking about universal human experience, which applies to any reader's understanding of their own emotional vocabulary.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that lexical distinctions are philosophical tools, not just a list of words.
review.appeal: +8 — it has a hook (four words for sadness), it is about a universal human experience, and it can be read with no background, though it may be more appealing to language lovers.

zh.thesis: 阿拉伯语中多个表示悲伤的词语，反映了情感与语言、文化之间的深层关系。
paragraphs: 阿拉伯语中有四个词来表示悲伤，每种都有细微差别，这并非偶然。
哲学指出，语言不仅描述情感，还塑造情感体验。
丰富的词汇让我们能更细致地理解和表达情感。
这个例子说明，不同文化对情感的分类方式各异，而语言是理解世界的窗口。

en.thesis: The multiple Arabic words for sadness reflect a deep relationship between emotion, language, and culture.
paragraphs: Arabic has four words for sadness, each with its own nuance, which is not accidental.
Philosophy suggests that language does not just describe emotions but shapes how we experience them.
A rich vocabulary allows us to understand and express feelings more precisely.
This example shows that different cultures categorize emotions differently, and language is a window to understanding the world.

articles.title: ‘There are 1.5 sex scenes, and the food looks just fine’
articles.titleZh: 电影《托尼》与布尔丹的「坏小子」形象
articles.author: Vittles

review.argument: Argument: it claims the film Tony fails to capture Bourdain's appetite and complexity, reducing his origin story to an anodyne coming-of-age tale, and contrasts it with the lusty, sensualist memoir it adapts.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a biopic flattens a larger-than-life figure into a generic template, and the reader can apply this to any adaptation or origin story. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the critical judgment, not just the plot summary.
review.appeal: +5 — it has a hook (the '1.5 sex scenes' quip) and is about a cultural figure many know, but it is mostly for film and food culture readers.

zh.thesis: 新片《托尼》把布尔丹的早年生活拍成了无趣的成长故事，恰恰消解了他本人最迷人的特质。
paragraphs: 《厨房机密》是本黑暗幽默又充满欲望的书。书中写他第一次吃牡蛎，是「湿漉漉、隐约带着情色意味的东西」，充满感官与生命力。
但导演马特·约翰逊的《托尼》讲的不是布尔丹的胃口，而是一个讨人厌的中产少年在科德角打工洗盘子、追逐女孩的夏天。
基努·里维斯？不，是多米尼克·塞萨饰演的托尼，在海鲜店学开牡蛎，跟着主厨学守时，度过了平平无奇的暑假。
名人起源故事很难拍，需要在成名前种下日后人格的种子。但《托尼》刻意回避了布尔丹的猎奇、情欲与对人的非凡方式，只剩下温吞的成长。
所以这是一部把传奇拍成普通人的电影，却忘了布尔丹的传奇恰恰在于他从不普通。它的窄视角回避了故事的广度和复杂性，留下的是安全无害的怀旧。

en.thesis: The new film 'Tony' turns Bourdain's early life into a dull coming-of-age story, stripping away the very qualities that made him fascinating.
paragraphs: Kitchen Confidential is a darkly funny, lusty book. In it Bourdain writes of his first oyster as a 'glistening, vaguely sexual-looking object', full of sensory appetite.
But director Matt Johnson's Tony is not about Bourdain's appetite. It is about an obnoxious middle-class teenager spending a summer washing dishes in Provincetown, chasing a girl.
Dominic Sessa's Tony shucks oysters, learns punctuality from a chef (Antonio Banderas), and has an unremarkable summer.
Origin stories about famous people must plant the seeds of the persona before it forms. But Tony deliberately avoids Bourdain's curiosity, sexuality, and way with people, leaving only bland growth.

So this film turns a legend into an ordinary person, forgetting that Bourdain's legend was his refusal to be ordinary. Its narrow focus sidesteps the breadth and complexity of his life, leaving safe, harmless nostalgia.

rejected.title: The Best Ocean Photos of the Year

review.argument: Announcement: it reports the finalists of the Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026 awards and describes a selection of the images, with no contestable claim or argument beyond the contest's own promotional framing.
review.transfer: A non-specialist comes away with a sense of the contest's categories and a few striking images, but the piece is essentially a curated gallery; the transfer is minimal—it does not change how one thinks about oceans or photography.
review.claim: A list: the writer selects and describes photos, but delete the writer and you lose only the curation and captions, not an argument or judgment that could be disagreed with.
review.appeal: +5 — the images are inherently appealing and some facts (like the pygmy seahorse's size) are dinner-worthy, but the piece is inert and promotional, with no people or scenes beyond the photos themselves.

rejected.title: 我错过了多少泼天的富贵？

review.argument: Announcement: the author recounts a colleague's question about Nvidia financing GPU purchases and his own regret at not buying semiconductor funds earlier, capped with the aphorism that one cannot earn money beyond one's cognition.
